name: Red Team
summary: Offensive tooling for authorized penetration tests and red-team engagements
description: Credential attacks, exploitation helpers, Active Directory and Windows protocol tooling, and pivoting utilities for engagements you have written authorization to perform. Several cornerstone frameworks (Metasploit, Responder, NetExec, BloodHound, Sliver) are not in Debian main and are listed as external tools with vendor install instructions rather than bundled.

tools.name: THC Hydra
tools.summary: Parallelised network login brute-forcer for many protocols

tools.name: Medusa
tools.summary: Parallel, modular login brute-forcer for network services

tools.name: Ncrack
tools.summary: High-speed network authentication cracking tool from the Nmap project

tools.name: Patator
tools.summary: Multi-purpose brute-forcer with fine-grained control

tools.name: John the Ripper
tools.summary: Offline password hash cracker with many formats

tools.name: hashcat
tools.summary: GPU-accelerated password recovery for a wide range of hashes
tools.notes: GPU acceleration needs the appropriate OpenCL driver for your hardware; without it hashcat falls back to the CPU.

tools.name: hashID
tools.summary: Identify the type of a given password hash

tools.name: crunch
tools.summary: Generate wordlists from a character set and pattern

tools.name: CeWL
tools.summary: Build a target-specific wordlist by spidering a website

tools.name: Impacket
tools.summary: Python classes and example scripts for Windows network protocols
tools.notes: Ships many impacket-* example scripts (secretsdump, wmiexec, psexec, GetUserSPNs and more); the command shown is one of them.

tools.name: ldapdomaindump
tools.summary: Dump Active Directory information over LDAP into readable reports

tools.name: Kerberos clients
tools.summary: MIT Kerberos tools (kinit, klist) for AD ticket handling

tools.name: smbmap
tools.summary: Enumerate SMB shares and permissions across a network

tools.name: polenum
tools.summary: Retrieve the password policy from a Windows host over SMB

tools.name: FreeRDP
tools.summary: Remote Desktop Protocol client for reaching Windows hosts

tools.name: Weevely
tools.summary: Generate and manage a stealthy PHP web shell

tools.name: THC-IPv6
tools.summary: Toolkit for attacking and testing IPv6 and ICMPv6
tools.notes: Ships many separate programs named atk6-* (e.g. atk6-alive6, atk6-parasite6); see the package's file list for the full set.

tools.name: ProxyChains-NG
tools.summary: Force a program's connections through a chain of proxies

tools.name: sshuttle
tools.summary: Transparent proxy and VPN over an SSH connection for pivoting

tools.name: iodine
tools.summary: Tunnel IPv4 traffic through a DNS server to bypass filtering

tools.name: Aircrack-ng
tools.summary: Suite for monitoring and testing Wi-Fi (WEP/WPA) security
tools.notes: Monitor-mode capture needs a wireless adapter and driver that support it.

tools.name: Wifite
tools.summary: Automate wireless auditing using the aircrack-ng tools

tools.name: Reaver
tools.summary: Brute-force Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) PINs

tools.name: hcxdumptool
tools.summary: Capture WPA key material from Wi-Fi devices for offline cracking

tools.name: hcxtools
tools.summary: Convert Wi-Fi captures into hashcat and John formats

external.name: Metasploit Framework
external.summary: Widely used exploitation and payload development framework
external.license: BSD-3-Clause for the framework; the Rapid7 installer and some content have their own terms.

why.text: The framework is not packaged in Debian; Rapid7 ships its own cross-distribution installer and nightly builds and expects to be updated from there.

how.text: Install the official omnibus package or nightly build from Rapid7's documented instructions for Linux, then update with msfupdate.

external.name: NetExec
external.summary: Network execution and enumeration across SMB, WinRM, LDAP and more
external.license: BSD-2-Clause (open source), successor to CrackMapExec; not packaged in Debian.

why.text: NetExec is maintained outside Debian and changes rapidly; upstream recommends installing it with pipx into an isolated environment.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx (pipx is in Debian): pipx install git+https://github.com/Pennyw0rth/NetExec.

external.name: Evil-WinRM
external.summary: WinRM shell for authenticated access to Windows hosts
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source), distributed as a Ruby gem; not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Evil-WinRM is published as a Ruby gem and is not packaged in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install the gem with 'gem install evil-winrm' (Ruby is in Debian), or run it from the official git checkout.

external.name: Responder
external.summary: LLMNR, NBT-NS and MDNS poisoner for credential capture
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source), not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Responder is free software but is not in Debian; it runs directly from a git checkout with Python 3.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run Responder.py; it uses only the Python 3 standard library.

external.name: BloodHound
external.license: Apache-2.0 (Community Edition) with a separate commercial Enterprise edition.

why.text: BloodHound Community Edition ships as container images and release bundles outside Debian; collectors are distributed with it.

how.text: Run BloodHound Community Edition from the official Docker Compose deployment, and collect data with SharpHound or BloodHound.py.

external.name: Sliver
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source), not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Sliver is released as prebuilt binaries by Bishop Fox and is not packaged in Debian.

how.text: Download the official server and client release binaries for Linux from the Sliver releases page and verify their signatures.
